headline: KSE-100 slips 206 points to 180,104 as Wall Street notches fresh record highs on cooling US inflation
mood: Mixed tape · Wall Street sets records, PSX consolidates, gold and oil retreat

five_things.html: The KSE-100 shed 206.60 points (-0.11%) to close at 180,104.61 on Thursday, snapping its two-day rebound as profit-taking hit fertiliser and pharmaceutical counters even as oil & gas exploration and cement names held firm; breadth turned negative with 269 decliners against 197 advancers (29 unchanged) on turnover of 388 million shares (Express Tribune, ARY News).

US equities extended their advance Thursday — the S&P 500 closed at a fresh record near 7,799 (+0.6%), the Nasdaq Composite jumped to 26,803.03 (+0.8%) and the Dow added 69.72 points (+0.13%) to 53,839.99 — after a flat July producer-price print reinforced bets the Fed will hold rates in September (CNBC, Detroit News).

The US, Iran and Oman are closing in on an interim arrangement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, though Tehran insists the waterway will not fully reopen until Washington agrees to end hostilities, withdraw forces and provide compensation — keeping a residual risk premium in oil markets even as Brent eased to $87.18 and WTI to $81.27 (Washington Post, Al Jazeera).

Gold slid 1.3% to $4,349.80/oz and silver fell 1.4% to $64.29/oz Thursday as a cooler-than-expected July PPI print eased Treasury yields and softened near-term safe-haven demand, even as both metals remain well above year-ago levels (Kitco).

Seven OPEC+ producers — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman — finalised a 188,000 bpd September output increase, completing the rollback of 2023's 1.65 million bpd voluntary cuts, while Saudi Arabia's non-oil private sector (Riyad Bank PMI) held expansionary at 53.1 in July even as export orders fell for a fifth straight month (Iraq Business News, Arab News).

matrix.local_html: The KSE-100 retreated 206.60 points (-0.11%) to close at 180,104.61 on Thursday, giving back part of Wednesday's rebound as fertiliser and pharmaceutical counters saw profit-taking while oil & gas exploration and cement held up; breadth turned negative with 269 decliners against 197 advancers and 29 unchanged on turnover of 388 million shares, led by CNERGY, BOP, KEL and SSGC (Express Tribune). The exchange is now closed for an extended weekend around Pakistan's Independence Day, with trading resuming Monday. The SBP held its policy rate at 11.5% at its July 27 review for a second straight pause, with July CPI at 9.2% y/y even as food inflation ran hotter at 10.6% (Business Recorder). Six-month KIBOR stood at roughly 11.51/11.76% as of August 7 (SBP). The interbank USD/PKR held broadly steady at 277.65, up a marginal one paisa on the day (Business Recorder). On the IMF front, an EFF/RSF review mission is due in Islamabad next month, with Pakistan eyeing roughly $1.2bn combined — about $1bn under the EFF and $200m under the climate-focused RSF — with circular debt, structural reforms and privatisation progress the key tests (ProPakistani).
matrix.gcc_html: OPEC+ has finalised a further 188,000 bpd output increase for September — the alliance's sixth straight monthly hike this year — completing the rollback of the 2023 voluntary cuts, with the eight-nation group next due to meet on September 6 to assess Hormuz-linked risk (Iraq Business News). Saudi Arabia's non-oil private sector stayed in solid expansion for a fourth straight month, with the Riyad Bank PMI easing slightly to 53.1 in July from 53.3 in June as domestic demand strengthened even as export orders fell for a fifth consecutive month on high freight costs (Arab News, AGBI). The PIF, chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, has approved its 2026–2030 strategy, pivoting from rapid asset growth toward value creation with tourism, travel and entertainment as priority sectors under Vision 2030 (PIF).
matrix.global_html: US equities closed at fresh records Thursday — the S&P 500 rose roughly 0.6% to about 7,799, the Nasdaq Composite jumped 0.8% to 26,803.03 and the Dow added 69.72 points (+0.13%) to 53,839.99 — after a flat July producer-price print reinforced bets the Fed will hold rates in September, with market-implied odds of a hike easing to roughly 40% from about 50% a day earlier (CNBC). The 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 4.66% and the 2-year held near 4.16% on the softer inflation read (Trading Economics). Brent and WTI eased to $87.18 and $81.27 respectively as investors await clarity on a prospective US-Iran-Oman arrangement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, even as Tehran insists on further concessions before a full reopening (Washington Post). Gold and silver pulled back from recent highs, easing 1.3% to $4,349.80/oz and 1.4% to $64.29/oz respectively, as cooling yields reduced near-term safe-haven demand (Kitco).

legislative.impact_html: Wins: banks and FX reserves if the tranche clears, sovereign risk premium eases. Loses: energy consumers facing tariff/circular-debt adjustment conditionality, importers if reform slippage pressures the PKR.

legislative.impact_html: Wins: rate-sensitive and growth equities, EM currencies including the PKR. Loses: US dollar bulls and money-market yield-seekers as hike odds recede further.

levels.support_note: Thursday's intraday low; deeper support at 179,500 (desk estimate)
levels.resistance_note: Wednesday's close; a reclaim opens the path to Thursday's intraday high near 181,434

desk_stance_html: We read Thursday's modest 206-point pullback as consolidation rather than a trend reversal — breadth was negative and fertiliser/pharma saw profit-taking, but oil & gas exploration and cement held firm, and the index remains less than 1% off Wednesday's multi-day high. With the exchange closed for an extended Independence Day weekend, Monday's reopening should take its cues from how the Hormuz talks and September Fed-hike odds evolve over the break. A close back above 180,311 would reopen the path toward Thursday's 181,434 intraday high; a slip below 180,036 would point to a retest of 179,500. Oil & gas exploration, cement and commercial banks are the counters to watch for confirmation on the reopen. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.

KSE-100 slips 206 points to 180,104 even as Wall Street notches fresh record highs on cooling US inflation.

THE OVERNIGHT TAPE
US equities closed at fresh records Thursday — S&P 500 +0.6% to a record near 7,799, Nasdaq +0.8% to 26,803.03, Dow +0.13% (69.72 pts) to 53,839.99 — after a flat July producer-price print reinforced bets the Fed will hold rates in September. Market-implied odds of a September hike eased to roughly 40% from about 50% a day earlier, and the 10-year Treasury yield slipped to about 4.66% (2-year near 4.16%). Brent and WTI eased to $87.18 and $81.27 as markets await clarity on a prospective US-Iran-Oman arrangement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Gold and silver pulled back from recent highs, easing 1.3% to $4,349.80/oz and 1.4% to $64.29/oz as cooling yields softened near-term safe-haven demand.

PAKISTAN
The KSE-100 shed 206.60 points (-0.11%) to close at 180,104.61, giving back part of Wednesday's rebound as fertiliser and pharmaceutical counters saw profit-taking while oil & gas exploration and cement held up. Breadth turned negative with 269 decliners against 197 advancers (29 unchanged) on turnover of 388 million shares, led by CNERGY, BOP, KEL and SSGC. The exchange is now closed for an extended Independence Day weekend, reopening Monday. SBP held its policy rate at 11.5% for a second straight review, with July CPI at 9.2% even as food inflation ran hotter at 10.6%. Six-month KIBOR stood near 11.51/11.76% as of August 7. USD/PKR interbank held broadly steady at 277.65. An IMF EFF/RSF review mission is due in Islamabad next month, with Pakistan eyeing roughly $1.2bn combined, with circular debt and privatisation progress the key tests.

GCC
OPEC+ finalised a further 188,000 bpd output increase for September, completing the rollback of 2023's voluntary cuts, with the group next due to meet September 6. Saudi Arabia's non-oil PMI eased slightly to 53.1 in July (from 53.3) but stayed firmly expansionary for a fourth straight month, even as export orders fell for a fifth month on high freight costs. The PIF, chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, has approved its 2026–2030 strategy, pivoting toward value creation with tourism, travel and entertainment as priority sectors under Vision 2030.

GLOBAL
A benign US producer-price print and a nearing Hormuz endgame are the two swing factors reshaping global risk sentiment. Washington, Tehran and Muscat are closing in on an interim arrangement to reopen the Strait, though Iran insists on further concessions before a full reopening.

LEGISLATIVE TRACKER
• Pakistan: 5th IMF EFF/RSF review due next month (~$1.2bn at stake) — wins: banks, FX reserves, sovereign risk; loses: energy consumers facing tariff conditionality.
• GCC: OPEC+ finalises 188,000 bpd September hike, next review Sept 6; PIF's 2026–2030 strategy backs tourism/entertainment — wins: oil-importing economies, Saudi non-oil diversification plays; loses: OPEC+ producers' per-barrel revenue.
• Global: flat July PPI pulls September Fed-hike odds to ~40% — wins: rate-sensitive equities, EM FX including the PKR; loses: USD bulls, money-market yield-seekers.

THE DAY AHEAD
KSE-100 support 180,036 (deeper support 179,500) · pivot 180,105 (Thursday's close) · resistance 180,311 (Wednesday's close), then Thursday's 181,434 intraday high. We read this as consolidation, not reversal — a close back above 180,311 reopens the path toward record territory; a slip below 180,036 points to a retest of 179,500. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.
